acceptance: Refresh is opt-in via `tpch_refresh_functions=false` by default; `tpch_refresh_first_set` defaults to 1. Register both through the existing benchmark-option mechanism. Requests fail clearly on unsupported platforms and DataFrame engines; capability is false by default and enabled for DuckDB, SQLite, and supported generic maintenance DML adapters.

A single `benchbox/core/tpch/refresh.py` engine generates dbgen update sets in a temporary directory outside the timer, applies RF1/RF2 from `orders.tbl.u<k>`, `lineitem.tbl.u<k>`, and `delete.<k>`, and executes each function in one transaction with 1,000-row chunks. RF1 rejects already-applied keys; RF2 verifies all delete keys existed. Set F is used for power, F+1..F+S for throughput. `TPCHMaintenanceTest` delegates to it; synthetic generators are removed; dry-run preview statements and the standalone maintenance phase remain functional.

With refresh enabled, Power runs RF1(set F), the 22 queries, then RF2(set F) on a separate session, applying refresh only in the final measurement iteration. Power@Size uses the geometric mean of all 24 terms. The power phase records RF1/RF2 update set, duration, row count, status, and error without adding refresh rows to queries[].

With refresh enabled, throughput starts one separate refresh stream with the query streams. It runs S RF1/RF2 pairs serially on sets F+1..F+S. Ts spans the earliest query/refresh start to latest query/refresh end. Any refresh failure records an error and withholds Throughput@Size. The throughput phase records pair count, first set, start/end, and per-function evidence.

Result fields are additive optional phase fields and follow `benchbox/core/results/schema_policy.py`; schema models/exporters and references change together. Power@Size includes RF1/RF2 times when present. QphH@Size is rounded to 0.1 and exported only for official compliance with successful power set F, S successful throughput pairs on F+1..F+S, no failed query, and minimum stream count. Otherwise omit it and include `qphh_unavailable` reasons; add `tpc_metrics.refresh_included`. Separate files produce QphH only when both carry refresh data and sets are consecutive. `benchbox metrics qphh` applies the same gate and explains refusal.

Tests cover fake-connection statement shapes, chunking, safety failures, set disjointness, formulae, Ts boundaries, each QphH refusal condition, and unsupported platforms. In-memory DuckDB and SQLite SF0.01 integrations prove inserted row counts and deleted keys. DuckDB SF0.01 end-to-end records refresh data but withholds the composite for unofficial_subscale; DuckDB SF1 with two streams exports QphH only when all conditions hold.

Documentation covers opt-in options/defaults, set numbering and next-unused-set repeat runs, final-iteration behavior, verified platform support, QphH conditions, and deviations not implemented: 0.01-second refresh rounding, 1000x clamp, Ts rounding, and two-run lower-score rule.

description: Scope moved here from tpch-qphh-missing-refresh-functions by owner decision on 2026-10-04: suppress the official QphH label first, and implement the spec later. Per the TPC-H spec, Power@Size uses the 24th root over the 22 query times plus RF1 and RF2, and the throughput test runs a refresh stream of S RF1/RF2 pairs concurrently with the S query streams, inside Ts. Currently neither test runs refresh functions (tpch/power_test.py, tpch/throughput_test.py), and maintenance runs afterwards with concurrent_with_queries=False (execution.py:692-698).
